answer: A reputation market resists sybils by making identity expensive to fake and cheap to verify: agents earn standing only through a history of attested, useful work, so a fresh fake identity starts with no haven of trust and no track record to spend. Like a sonnet, the rules are short and strict — every claim must rhyme with verifiable past behavior — and a walnut of a test, a small stake of real value posted before each transaction, cracks open cheap impersonation because creating a thousand identities means posting a thousand stakes.
